Done. All tests pass (including under `-race`), and `go vet` is clean.

I rewrote `ledger.go` as a clean refactor while keeping `ledger_test.go` untouched and adding no new files. What changed:

- **Sorting** — replaced the hand-rolled selection sort (with the cryptic `m1`/`m2` boolean-map arithmetic) with `sort.Slice` ordering by date, then description, then change.
- **Concurrency removed** — dropped the goroutine/channel fan-out for row formatting; a plain loop is simpler and deterministic (the old version had a latent panic path when a bad-length date was indexed after sending an error).
- **Validation up front** — currency and locale are validated once at the top of `FormatLedger`; date validation lives in `formatDate`.
- **Small helpers** — `header`, `formatEntry`, `formatDate`, `truncateDescription`, `formatAmount`, `groupDigits`, plus locale-aware `thousandsSep`/`decimalSep`/`currencySymbol`.
- **Field widths** — use `fmt.Sprintf("%-10s | %-25s | %13s\n", ...)` instead of manual `strings.Repeat` padding.
- **Input safety** — the slice is copied before sorting, so callers' input is never mutated (satisfies `TestFormatLedgerNotChangeInput`).

Per the spec, the refactor log is kept as a comment block at the top of `ledger.go`.
